conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I'm feeling pretty frustrated. Just the other day, I walked past a park where I used to hang out, and suddenly it all came flooding back—memories I thought I could handle just hit me out of nowhere. It's exhausting to keep reliving those moments.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds really tough to deal with. Can you tell me how long the feelings from those memories lasted?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: It was intense for a good while. I found myself stuck in those thoughts for hours, replaying everything again and again like a broken record. Even afterward, I couldn't shake the heaviness; it lingered well into the night, making it hard to sleep.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It sounds draining to have that heaviness affect your sleep. When you were trying to sleep, did you notice any specific thoughts or feelings that were particularly strong?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Yeah, so when I finally tried to lay down, my mind kept racing. I felt this deep sense of unease, like I was waiting for something bad to happen, even though nothing was going on. It was frustrating because I wanted to rest, but my brain just wouldn't let me.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds really uncomfortable. During the day, did you notice any moments where that sense of unease came up again?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Definitely. Just the other day, I was in a coffee shop, and I suddenly felt that familiar churn in my stomach. The noise around me, the clatter of cups, brought back a flash of a chaotic moment that I thought I had buried. It made me want to just leave and find a quiet spot away from everyone.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It sounds like that experience in the coffee shop was really unsettling. How did you cope with that feeling in the moment?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Honestly, I didn’t cope very well at all. I ended up just sitting there, trying to distract myself with my phone, but it felt like nothing was working. I kept glancing at the door, half hoping to find an escape rather than facing that uncomfortable feeling.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: Feeling trapped in that situation can be really tough. Did you notice how your thoughts changed while you were waiting there?
